data.name: Barclay
data.gender_notes: Barclay is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from Old English 'bear' and 'clif' or Old Norse 'barkr' and 'leikr' meaning 'son of barley' or 'stony clearing'. In the Bible, Barclay could refer to Barclay the son of Abaddon mentioned in the book of Numbers. The name also has connections to St. Bartholomew, one of the twelve apostles. The name Barclay carries the meaning “Son of barley” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Barclay usually hope their child will grow to embody son of barley and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of nourishment and sustenance, representing the bounty and abundance of God's providence.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Barclay total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.
